label: lem:strongly_measurable_interior
title: Strong measurability at interior points
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, and let $x \in (\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$. Then $f$ is strongly measurable at the neighborhood filter of $x$ within $\mathrm{Ioi}\; x$ (i.e.\ \texttt{StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f (nhdsWithin x (Ioi x))}). This follows because the interior of $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ is open and belongs to the Lebesgue measurable sets.
proof: Since $x$ lies in the open interior $(\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$, there is an open neighborhood of $x$ contained in the domain. Continuous functions on open sets are strongly measurable with respect to the Lebesgue measure, giving measurability at the neighborhood filter.
